title: Nika project file · nika.yaml · v1
description: Structural contract for a project's `nika.yaml`: the project's name, its default spend ceiling, the team arming registry (`arm:`), the trace retention policy and the registry provenance floor. The grammar is closed — an unknown key anywhere is a named refusal — and every value form below is the one the parser accepts; the beat keys keep the French spellings the parser reads (`où` · `manqué` · `après_saut` · …) and each is described here in English.

nika.description: The project's name — kebab-case opening with a letter (`my-project`). The retired schema tag (`v1`, `v2`, …) is refused: the version lives on the `$schema` line.

ceiling.description: The default `--max-cost-usd` for every run in this project (USD). A run may lower it, never raise it silently.

arm.description: The team arming registry: the beats the resident (`nika serve`) fires on their cadence. Validated by every door, fired by one.

workflow.description: The workflow file, relative to the project root (`workflows/nightly.nika`).

cadence.description: When the beat fires, its IANA zone first: five cron fields (`TZ=Europe/Paris 0 9 * * 1`), a French weekday and its time (`TZ=Europe/Paris lundi 9h07`), an anchored interval (`TZ=Europe/Paris every 2 weeks from 2026-10-05 09:00`), or `on-webhook`, the one form with no zone. The zone is required for every scheduled form; `nika check`, `nika arm` and `nika serve` refuse a cadence without it.

où.description: Where the beat runs: `local` (this machine's resident) or `cloud` (a remote resident).

plafond.description: Required, with no default: the beat's spend ceiling in USD for each fire (`--max-cost-usd`). Choosing for the operator would be choosing who pays.

manqué.description: Required, with no default: what a missed slot becomes when the firer comes back. `rattraper` fires the latest missed slot once; `{ rattraper: N }` fires up to the N latest missed slots, one run each, oldest first, so the activation shows the worst cost as « jusqu'à N × plafond »; `rattraper-une-fois` fires once, that run answering for every missed slot; `sauter` skips them. Each run receives the slot it fires for.

rattraper.description: How many of the latest missed slots to fire, one run each, oldest first: a whole number from 1.

chevauchement.description: What a new slot does while the previous fire still runs: `sauter` (skip it), `file` (queue it), `remplacer` (replace the running one).

après_saut.description: When the beat resumes after a skipped slot: at the next slot (`prochain-créneau`) or when the running fire completes (`à-complétion`).

actif.description: Whether the beat is armed. A suspended beat (`false`) must say why in `raison`.

raison.description: Why the beat is suspended, verbatim. Required with `actif: false`.

jusqu_au.description: The date that bounds a suspension: an ISO calendar date (`2026-12-31`), nothing else. Required with `actif: false`.

tolérance.description: The (m,k)-firm skip tolerance (`3/4`). Accepted in the file, refused at apply and load until the (m,k) law exists.

décalage.description: `hash`, the one value: a deterministic offset derived from the workflow path. Accepted in the file; both firers refuse it until the jitter law exists.

par.description: Who armed the beat, verbatim (a name, a handle) — the provenance line the ledger reads.

inputs.description: Per-beat inputs: the `--var KEY=VALUE` pairs every fire binds to the workflow's declared `inputs:` — one scalar per key, coerced by the declared type at admission (a typed array input takes its JSON text in quotes). A key the workflow does not declare refuses before the claim.

keep.description: The retention age cap (`30d`): a trace older than this exits even under the keep-N window. A paused trace is never collected.

registry.description: The registry provenance admission floor — a gate on what the project installs.

floor.description: Refuse artifacts below this provenance tier: `unprovenanced` (digest-consistent) · `provenanced` (minisign-verified under the publisher's key) · `stage-clear` (a staged-window statement) · `verified` (a complete in-toto layout).
